title: Plane Shapes and Solid Shapes
seo_title: Plane and Solid Shapes – JSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Identify the properties of plane shapes (triangles and quadrilaterals) and of solids (cubes, cuboids, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones and spheres); draw and recognise nets. (summary of the NERDC JSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 1 maths worksheets on plane shapes and solids: properties of triangles and quadrilaterals, faces, edges and vertices of solids, and nets. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Plane shapes are flat; solids have 3 dimensions
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A parallelogram has opposite sides equal and parallel; a rhombus has all four sides equal; a trapezium has one pair of parallel sides.
  • A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices.
  • A net is a flat pattern that folds into a solid.

Examples

Example

Square-based pyramid

1 square + 4 triangles

Answer: 5 faces, 8 edges, 5 vertices

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking a square is not a rectangleA square is a special rectangle.
Counting the same edge twiceMark edges as you count.
Calling a cone a pyramidA cone has a circular base.

faq.a: A closed plane shape with straight sides.

faq.q: How many faces has a cylinder?
faq.a: Three: two flat and one curved.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle, so it is a right triangle. The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is isosceles. Its full name is right isosceles triangle. The other 2 angles are acute, but a triangle is named by its largest angle.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle, so it is a right triangle. There are no tick marks: all 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. Its full name is right scalene triangle.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: One angle is wider than a right angle, so it is obtuse. The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is isosceles. Its full name is obtuse isosceles triangle. Having 2 acute angles does not make it acute: look at the largest angle.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: All 3 angles are smaller than a right angle, so it is acute. There are no tick marks: all 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. Its full name is acute scalene triangle.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: One angle is wider than a right angle, so it is obtuse. There are no tick marks: all 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. Its full name is obtuse scalene triangle. Turning a triangle does not change its name.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: All 3 angles are smaller than a right angle, so it is acute. The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is isosceles. Its full name is acute isosceles triangle. Only 2 sides have tick marks, so it is not equilateral. Standing on its point does not change its name.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle, so it is a right triangle. There are no tick marks: all 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. Its full name is right scalene triangle. Turning a triangle does not change its name.

items.q: Which names fit this triangle?
items.e: The tick marks show 3 equal sides, so it is equilateral. An isosceles triangle has at least 2 equal sides, and this one has 3, so it is isosceles too.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides.
items.e: The tick marks show 2 equal sides, so it is isosceles. The third side has no tick mark, so it is not equilateral. (Obtuse describes an angle, and this triangle has no obtuse angle.)

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides.
items.e: There are no tick marks and the 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. (Right describes an angle, and this triangle has no right angle.)

items.q: Which is a right isosceles triangle?
items.e: Triangle D has a right angle (the small square) and 2 equal sides (the tick marks). The other right triangle is scalene, and the other isosceles triangles are acute and obtuse.

items.q: Which triangle is scalene?
items.e: Triangle B has no equal sides, so it is scalene. The others have tick marks on at least 2 sides, so they are isosceles (one is also equilateral).

items.q: A triangle has angles of 100°, 40° and 40°. Classify it by its angles.
items.e: 100° is more than 90°, so it is an obtuse triangle. Every triangle has at least 2 acute angles, so name it by its largest angle.

items.q: A triangle has three 60° angles. Classify it by its angles.
items.e: 60° is less than 90°, so all 3 angles are acute: it is an acute triangle. (Equilateral is a name by sides, not by angles.)

items.q: A triangle has sides of 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm. Classify it by its sides.
items.e: 2 sides are 5 cm, so it has 2 equal sides. That makes it isosceles.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 4 m, 7 m and 9 m. Classify it by its sides.
items.e: All 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene.

items.q: Can a right triangle also be an obtuse triangle?
c: No, only 1 angle can be 90° or more
items.e: A right angle and an obtuse angle together are already more than 180°, the total of a triangle's angles. So a triangle has at most 1 angle that is 90° or more.

items.q: Can a right triangle be isosceles?
items.e: A right isosceles triangle has a right angle and 2 equal sides, like half of a square cut corner to corner.

items.q: Which is a right isosceles triangle?
items.e: Triangle C has a right angle (the small square) and 2 equal sides (the tick marks). The other right triangle is scalene, and the other isosceles triangles are acute and obtuse.

items.q: Which triangle is scalene?
items.e: Triangle D has no equal sides, so it is scalene. The others have tick marks on at least 2 sides, so they are isosceles (one is also equilateral).

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides and the small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a square. It is also a rhombus, a rectangle and a parallelogram, but square tells the most. Turning it on a corner does not make it a different shape.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle. Only opposite sides are equal, so it is not a square. It is also a parallelogram, but rectangle tells more.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. It has no right angles, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. It has no right angles, so it is not a square. Standing it on a point does not change its name.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram. It has no right angles (not a rectangle) and its sides are not all equal (not a rhombus).

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezium, not a parallelogram.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezium, not a parallelogram. It has 2 right angles, but a rectangle needs 4.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 2 pairs of equal sides next to each other, so it is a kite. Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus, and it has no parallel sides.

items.q: Which name does NOT fit this shape?
items.e: It has 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle, a parallelogram and a quadrilateral. Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus.

items.q: Which name does NOT fit this shape?
items.e: It has 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus, a parallelogram and a quadrilateral. It has no right angles, so it is not a rectangle.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is both a rectangle and a rhombus, so it goes where the two boxes overlap: region 5, the squares. A square belongs to every box: rectangles, rhombuses, parallelograms and quadrilaterals.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 right angles. Its sides are 8 cm, 3 cm, 8 cm and 3 cm. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is a rectangle but not a rhombus (its sides are not all equal), so it goes in region 3.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides and no right angles. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is a rhombus but not a rectangle (no right angles), so it goes in region 4.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 2 pairs of parallel sides, no right angles, and sides of 9 cm, 5 cm, 9 cm and 5 cm. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is a parallelogram, but it has no right angles and its sides are not all equal. So it is not a rectangle or a rhombus: region 2.

items.q: A quadrilateral has exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is a quadrilateral but not a parallelogram, so it goes in region 1, outside the Parallelograms box. With only 1 pair of parallel sides it is a trapezium, not a parallelogram.

items.q: A square is turned so that it stands on one corner. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is both a rectangle and a rhombus, so it goes where the two boxes overlap: region 5, the squares. Turning does not change its sides or angles, so it is still a square.

items.q: A kite has 2 short equal sides, 2 long equal sides, and no parallel sides. In which region of the diagram does it belong?
items.e: It is a quadrilateral but not a parallelogram, so it goes in region 1, outside the Parallelograms box. A kite like this has no parallel sides at all.

items.q: Which region holds the shapes that are both rectangles and rhombuses?
items.e: Region 5 is where the Rectangles box and the Rhombuses box overlap. These shapes have 4 right angles and 4 equal sides: they are the squares.

items.q: Regions 3 and 5 together make up which group?
items.e: The Rectangles box covers region 3 and region 5. So every square (region 5) is a rectangle.

items.q: Regions 4 and 5 together make up which group?
items.e: The Rhombuses box covers region 4 and region 5. So every square (region 5) is a rhombus.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 6 rectangular faces, and they are not all squares, so it is a cuboid.

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: It has a square base and 4 triangle faces that meet at one vertex, so it is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 4 faces and all of them are triangles, so it is a tetrahedron (a triangular-based pyramid).
It has 2 flat circular faces and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder. A circle is a 2-D shape.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: The two end faces are hexagons (6 sides) joined by rectangles, so it is a hexagonal prism. A hexagon is a 2-D shape.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: How many vertices does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: How many vertices does a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: How many edges does a cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: This is a tetrahedron. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: How many edges does a tetrahedron have?
items.e: A tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

items.q: This is a hexagonal prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons and 6 rectangles), 18 edges and 12 vertices. Faces are the flat surfaces, edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners. Dashed lines show the edges you cannot see.

items.q: I am a 3-D shape with 6 faces. All of my faces are squares of the same size. What am I?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces that are all equal squares. A cuboid has rectangular faces.

items.q: I have 5 faces: 1 square and 4 triangles. What am I?
items.e: 1 square base and 4 triangles that meet at the top make a square-based pyramid.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has 4 faces, and all of them are triangles?
items.e: A tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. A square-based pyramid has a square face as well.

items.q: What shape are the faces of a cuboid?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces (some of them can be squares, which are special rectangles).

items.q: Which of these 3-D shapes has no vertices?
items.e: A sphere is round all over: it has no flat faces, no edges and no vertices (corners).

items.q: How many faces does a cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices: 6.

items.q: How many faces does a cone have?
items.e: A cone has 2 faces, 1 edges and 1 vertices: 2.

items.q: How many vertices (corners) does a cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices: 8.

items.q: How many vertices (corners) does a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices: 5.

items.q: How many edges does a cone have?
items.e: A cone has 2 faces, 1 edges and 1 vertices: 1.

items.q: How many edges does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices: 9.

items.q: How many faces does a cube have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices: 6.

items.q: How many faces does a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices: 5.

items.q: How many vertices (corners) does a cube have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices: 8.

items.q: How many faces does a cylinder have?
items.e: A cylinder has 3 faces, 2 edges and 0 vertices: 3.

items.q: How many vertices (corners) does a cone have?
items.e: A cone has 2 faces, 1 edges and 1 vertices: 1.

items.q: How many edges does a cylinder have?
items.e: A cylinder has 3 faces, 2 edges and 0 vertices: 2.

items.q: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices: 5.

items.q: How many faces does a tetrahedron (triangular-based pyramid) have?
items.e: A tetrahedron (triangular-based pyramid) has 4 faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices: 4.

items.q: How many vertices (corners) does a tetrahedron (triangular-based pyramid) have?
items.e: A tetrahedron (triangular-based pyramid) has 4 faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices: 4.

items.q: How many edges does a tetrahedron (triangular-based pyramid) have?
items.e: A tetrahedron (triangular-based pyramid) has 4 faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices: 6.

items.q: How many edges does a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices: 8.

items.q: How many edges does a cube have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices: 12.

items.q: How many vertices (corners) does a cylinder have?
items.e: A cylinder has 3 faces, 2 edges and 0 vertices: 0.

items.q: How many vertices (corners) does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices: 6.

items.q: Which 3-D shape does this net make?
items.e: There are 6 squares that are all the same size. They fold into a cube.

items.q: This net is folded up. What shape does it make?
items.e: There are 6 squares that are all the same size. They fold into a cube.

items.q: Which 3-D shape does this net make?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs, and they are not all squares. They fold into a cuboid.

items.q: This net is folded up. What shape does it make?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs, and they are not all squares. They fold into a cuboid.

items.q: Which 3-D shape does this net make?
items.e: There are 2 triangles (the ends) and 3 rectangles. They fold into a triangular prism.

items.q: This net is folded up. What shape does it make?
items.e: There are 2 triangles (the ends) and 3 rectangles. They fold into a triangular prism.

items.q: Which 3-D shape does this net make?
items.e: There is 1 square (the base) and 4 triangles that meet at the top. They fold into a square-based pyramid.

items.q: This net is folded up. What shape does it make?
items.e: There are 4 triangles and nothing else. They fold into a tetrahedron (a triangular-based pyramid).

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: D is not a net of a cube: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face and one face is left open. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: B is not a net of a cube: 5 squares in a row wrap all the way round, so the first and last squares overlap. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: C is not a net of a cube: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face and one face is left open. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these IS a net of a cube?
items.e: A folds into a cube with no gaps or overlaps. In the others, two squares fold onto the same face (two squares on the same side of a row of 4, 5 squares in a row, or a 2-by-2 block).

items.q: Which of these IS a net of a cube?
items.e: C folds into a cube with no gaps or overlaps. In the others, two squares fold onto the same face (two squares on the same side of a row of 4, 5 squares in a row, or a 2-by-2 block).

items.q: Which net folds into a square-based pyramid?
items.e: B has 1 square and 4 triangles, one on each side of the square. The net with only 3 triangles leaves one side open; the others make a triangular prism and a tetrahedron.

items.q: Which net folds into a triangular prism?
items.e: D has 3 rectangles and 2 triangles, one triangle at each end. One wrong net has only 2 rectangles, one has both triangles at the same end, and one is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face E?
items.e: Faces E and D are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face A?
items.e: Fold the net: face E lands opposite face A. A face that touches A in the net (B, D) is next to it on the cube, never opposite.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face A?
items.e: Faces A and E are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: How many faces does a net of a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: 1 square base and 4 triangles: 1 + 4 = 5 faces.

items.q: Kelechi folds a net of 6 rectangles into a cuboid. How many edges does the cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 12 edges (and 6 faces and 8 vertices). 6 is the number of faces.
